summary: New Hampshire's AI laws target harms to children, such as HB 143 on chatbots encouraging minors toward self-harm, sex or violence (effective Jan 2026), and deepfakes. No frontier or catastrophic-risk action was found; AG John Formella opposed federal preemption in 2025 but did not sign the 2026 frontier letter.

items.title: HB 143 — AI chatbots and child endangerment
items.text: Makes it child endangerment for chatbot operators to encourage minors toward sexual conduct, drugs, self-harm or violence, with AG civil enforcement.

items.title: 36-AG NAAG letter opposing federal preemption of state AI laws
items.text: The New Hampshire attorney general joined the bipartisan letter urging Congress to reject a moratorium on state AI laws.

profile.headline: New Hampshire's Republican governor and Legislature now want a multi-year moratorium on AI data centers.

sections.text: Gov. Kelly Ayotte said on September 2, 2026 that she opposes a proposed data center in Bow and will put a multi-year data-center moratorium in her next budget, which could take effect no earlier than July 2027. Senate President Sharon Carson said on September 18, 2026 that the Senate would pursue a moratorium too.
Dartmouth partnered with Anthropic and AWS in December 2025 to give students and staff campus-wide access to Claude, the first Ivy League deployment at that scale.
Rep. Chris Pappas, running for Senate, said in September 2026 that "New Hampshire is not the right place for AI data centers."

New Hampshire has no hyperscale AI campus under construction. In April 2026 a federal filing pointed to a possible 350 MW data center at the former Merrimack Station coal plant in Bow, a 343-acre site owned by Granite Shore Power. As of September 2026 Eversource was running a feasibility study at the company's request.

In May 2026 a plan to turn a Nottingham warehouse into a data center was withdrawn after opposition. On September 9, 2026, Nottingham voters approved a 12-month data-center moratorium, 1,335 to 143. In September 2026 Gov. Kelly Ayotte said she opposes "putting any data center in the state of New Hampshire" and would put a multi-year moratorium in her budget, effective July 2027 at the earliest. Senate President Sharon Carson backed exploring a moratorium, and House Democrats proposed a 24-month pause.
